title: Humanctl vault snapshot
description: The generic, versioned interchange the Brain view renders. A producer (any external tool over any personal knowledge base) maps its own opinionated schema into this shape and writes one file; humanctl reads and renders it and never inspects the producer's source. No producer-specific ontology term is a field here: domain values travel as data inside `labels`/`annotations`/`spec`, never as named columns the viewer hardcodes.

apiVersion.description: The contract version, carried inside the document. The viewer keys behavior off this string and shows an 'unsupported snapshot' state rather than crashing on an unknown major. Additive, backward-compatible changes do not bump the major.

generatedAt.description: When the producer wrote this snapshot (ISO 8601).

source.description: Free-form, non-identifying label for the producer (for example 'markdown vault'). Never a path, never personal.

vitals.description: Headline counts for the health strip. All optional; the viewer renders whatever is present.

lastIngest.description: ISO 8601 or a short relative label like '2h'.

entities.description: The rows of the vault. Each entity is generic; the producer owns the mapping from its own schema into this shape.

queues.description: Pre-computed work queues. The producer decides membership and ordering; the viewer only renders.

views.description: Optional presentation hints owned by the producer, so the viewer stays dumb about the domain. A hint names which label/spec keys become columns, the default sort, and optional per-label-value tones. Delivered as data, never baked into viewer code.

kind.description: Generic discriminant, e.g. 'person' or 'org'. The viewer renders unknown kinds with generic columns.

id.description: Stable identity, e.g. derived from the source file path. Referenced by relations and queues as '<kind>:<id>' or the bare id.

labels.description: Small closed key/value map the viewer may group, filter, and color by WITHOUT knowing what any key means. A producer's ontology value (say a relationship tier) ships here as a value, never as a first-class schema field.

annotations.description: Arbitrary non-identifying metadata the viewer shows but never interprets (role, one-line context).

spec.description: Generic contact facets, all optional. Producer pre-computes any derived state (a resolved status, not a raw staleness rule). The viewer renders known keys and shows unknown ones in a generic key/value fallback.

lastContactAt.description: ISO 8601 date of last meaningful contact.

source.description: A generic source label (a note filename). Never an absolute path.

relations.description: Typed edge list, never inline nesting. targetRef points at another entity by '<kind>:<id>' or bare id.

columns.description: Ordered label/spec keys to render as columns. 'label' is the entity name.

labelTones.description: Optional per-label-value tone hints, e.g. { "group": { "inner": "accent", "dormant": "muted" } }. Tones are a generic palette role, never a raw color.
